ignored when sizing the magnitude + rtol, atol = tolerance_for(ref, compute_dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fnuz) + assert rtol == 2**-4 + assert atol == 256.0 + + +if __name__ == "__main__": + for name, fn in sorted(globals().items()): + if name.startswith("test_") and callable(fn): + fn() + print(f"ok {name}") + print("all tolerance tests passed") -- 2.54.0.windows.1 ```

title: [RFC]: Let a failed `checkAllclose` fail the test
body:
### Motivation. **In short:** `checkAllclose` already computes the right verdict and then throws it away. This proposes one opt-in, default-off flag so that verdict can reach an exit code. **Size: 64 added lines in `aiter/test_common.py`, no deletions.** Everything else in the patch is a new test file. **Default behaviour is unchanged.** The new path is unreachable unless a caller passes `strict=True` or sets `AITER_STRICT_ALLCLOSE=1`. The environment variable is ignored on `printLog=False` (autotuners, quiet wrappers), which still just return the ratio. Verify on CPU in one command, no GPU, ROCm or JIT build: `python op_tests/test_checkallclose_strict.py` (6 assertions). There is **no open parameter in this one** — nothing is needed beyond accept/reject. It is independent of #5031 and #5032, touches a disjoint file set, applies in any order, and is the only one of the three with no behavioural change, so it is the cheapest place to start. --- `checkAllclose` is the correctness check for essentially the whole op_test suite: 649 call sites across 132 files, 617 of them in `op_tests/`. When a comparison exceeds `tol_err_ratio` it logs ``` [checkAllclose atol=100 rtol=0.01 failed!] -->max abs delta:1712.0, delta details: 12.5% (5242880 of 41943040) elements ``` and returns the mismatch ratio. Every op_test discards that return value, so nothing raises and the process exits 0. The CI harness gates on exactly that exit code. From `.github/scripts/aiter_test.sh`: ```bash set -euo pipefail ... test_cmd=(timeout 60m python3 "$file") ... if ! "${test_cmd[@]}" 2>&1 | tee -a latest_test.log; then status="❌ Test failed" testFailed=true failedFiles+=("$file") else status="✅ Test passed" fi ``` The harness is wired correctly — `pipefail` is set, so the `tee` does not swallow the status. The gap is that the comparison function has no way to trip it. A test can print `failed!` on every shape it runs and still be recorded as `✅ Test passed`. This is not hypothetical. On unmodified `main`, on an MI300X: ``` $ python3 op_tests/test_moe_tkw1.py ... 6x "[checkAllclose atol=100 rtol=0.01 failed!]" $ echo $? 0 ``` `op_tests/test_moe.py` on the same tree prints six `warning!` lines (mismatch under `tol_err_ratio`) and also exits 0. Those `warning!` lines would **not** fail under strict mode. `failed!` means `percent > tol_err_ratio`; `warning!` means some elements mismatched but the ratio stayed at or below the gate. Strict mode raises only on `failed!`. Two escape hatches were added recently and they do raise — `catastrophic_check=True` and an explicit `max_abs_delta`. They are opt-in and cover a different case (NaN/Inf, or a delta above half the reference peak). In `op_tests/` they appear at 27 of 617 call sites, concentrated in eight GEMM tests: ``` 7 of 8 op_tests/test_gemm_a8w8.py 6 of 6 op_tests/test_gemm_a8w8_blockscale.py 5 of 5 op_tests/test_gemm_a16w16.py 4 of 4 op_tests/test_gemm_a8w8_blockscale_cktile_aq_rowmajor.py 2 of 2 op_tests/triton_tests/gemm/basic/test_gemm_afp8wfp8.py 1 of 4 op_tests/test_gemm_a4w4.py 1 of 1 op_tests/test_deepgemm.py 1 of 1 op_tests/test_batched_gemm_a8w8.py ``` The other 590 can only log. (`op_tests/test_gdn_prepare.py` forwards `max_abs_delta` through a `_quiet_check_allclose` wrapper, so a couple of those 590 do reach a raising configuration indirectly; the count is of options passed at the call site itself.) So the practical situation is that the suite's default correctness check cannot fail a build, and turning that around currently means editing 590 call sites. #### Every past instance of this depended on a person noticing Several closed reports are field instances of exactly this mechanism, and they make the case better than the synthetic reproducer does. In each one `checkAllclose` printed a failure, the script continued to the next configuration, and the process still exited 0: * **#600** (`test_moe_tkw1.py`) — `[checkAllclose atol=100 rtol=0.01 failed!]` on four consecutive configurations, max abs delta 216, 204 and 312, 3.9–6.2% of elements mismatched. The run walked through every remaining shape and printed each failure in turn. * **#456** (`test_moe.py`) — the same line with max abs delta 338 and 24.0% (5886 of 24576) of elements mismatched. The comparison immediately above it on the same shape reports `passed~` at the same tolerance, so a reader has to distinguish the two by eye. * **#455** (`test_moe_blockscale.py`) — `[checkAllclose atol=0.05 rtol=0.05 failed!]` at m=1, 2, 5 and 16, with 24.4% and 26.4% element mismatch on the first two, again running to completion. Those kernel bugs were all fixed, and the point here is narrower than "these bugs existed": in all three cases the harness had already computed the correct verdict and had it in hand. The only thing missing was a way for that verdict to reach an exit code. That is why the flag is proposed at the `checkAllclose` layer rather than per test. ### Proposed Change. Add one opt-in, default-off argument to `checkAllclose`, prototyped in the patch attached below. Default behaviour is unchanged. #### `strict` (bool or None, default `None`) ```python def checkAllclose( a, b, rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-2, tol_err_ratio=0.05, msg="", printNum=8, printLog=True, max_abs_delta=None, catastrophic_check=False, strict=None, # new ): ``` * `None` — read `AITER_STRICT_ALLCLOSE` from the environment, but only on the logging path. Autotuners call with `printLog=False` and need the ratio returned so they can rank candidates, so the environment variable never turns those call sites into exceptions. Quiet wrappers that pass `printLog=False` are in the same bucket: `AITER_STRICT_ALLCLOSE=1` does not arm them. * `True` / `False` — explicit, honoured on every path. When strict is on and `percent > tol_err_ratio` (the same predicate that prints `failed!`), the existing log line is emitted exactly as today and then an `AssertionError` is raised: ``` op_tests/test_moe_tkw1.py: checkAllclose failed: 12.5% (5242880 of 41943040) elements exceed rtol=0.01 atol=100, above tol_err_ratio=0.05, max abs delta 1712 ``` The raise uses `>` on every path, matching `failed!`. The pre-existing `printLog=False` branch still *returns* the ratio at `percent >= tol_err_ratio` so tuners keep their current ranking threshold; it only raises when the logging path would have said `failed!`. Catastrophic mismatches keep raising regardless of `strict`, as they do now. This is deliberately one flag rather than a change of default. It does **not** redden CI until a workflow sets the variable. The patch as written does not include that workflow change. One environment variable then arms every logging-path call site without touching them, and it can be enabled per-shard while the fallout is worked through. ### Feedback Period. Two weeks, or until the shard-by-shard baseline below is in hand. ### CC List. _Maintainers of `aiter/test_common.py` and `.github/scripts/aiter_test.sh`._ ### Any Other Things. #### Reproducers Both attached. Neither needs a patched tree. `checkallclose_exit_code.py` — CPU tensors, no GPU maths, a few seconds. Compares two tensors that disagree on half their elements by a factor of ten and exits 0: ``` $ python checkallclose_exit_code.py ; echo "exit=$?" repro: [checkAllclose atol=0.01 rtol=0.01 failed!] -->max abs delta:10.0, delta details: 50.0% (4096 of 8192) elements checkAllclose returned 0.5 and did not raise. Process is about to exit 0. CI records the file as passed. exit=0 ``` `stock_optest_exit_code.sh` — runs an unmodified op_test on a GPU, counts the `failed!` lines, and prints the exit code. `evidence_from_checkout.py` — reproduces the call-site census (649 / 617 / 27) from the source tree alone, no GPU and no torch. #### How this gets adopted The flag is useless if switching it on turns CI red everywhere, so the intended sequence is: 1. Land the flag with the default off. No behavioural change; the new `op_tests/test_checkallclose_strict.py` pins that. 2. Run the suite once per shard with `AITER_STRICT_ALLCLOSE=1` to get a baseline of which files would fail. This is the number that decides whether the remaining work is a handful of tolerance fixes or a real backlog. I do not have that baseline; it is the substance of the proposal rather than a formality. 3. Enable it per-shard in the workflow as each shard comes clean. What is known today is narrower: on stock `main`, `test_moe_tkw1.py` prints six `failed!` lines, so **that file** goes red the moment strict mode is switched on for its shard. `test_moe.py`'s six `warning!` lines would not. An earlier draft of this issue argued those particular failures were only miscalibrated tolerances, citing an offline re-decision of recorded comparisons that found no pass→fail flips. **That argument has since been withdrawn.** Running the companion tolerance patch from #5031 on an MI300X flipped the int8 MoE path from pass to fail, which exposed a defect in that derivation rather than in the kernel. Until #5031's tolerances are right, the question of whether the MoE `failed!` lines are tolerance artefacts or real is genuinely open. That is an argument for this flag, not against it: the baseline in step 2 is exactly how you find out, and today there is no way to collect it short of reading logs by eye. It is also the reason the flag ships default-off, and the reason I would land this one before #5031 — arming the gate is safe and reversible, while a mis-derived tolerance behind an armed gate is not. #### What this does not address Strict mode makes a *failed* comparison fail the build. It does nothing about comparisons that are set up so loosely that they cannot fail — `atol=100` in the MoE tests (#5031), or a whole-tensor average that dilutes localized corruption (#5032). #### Patch Against `536118a`. Inlined below rather than attached — I cannot fork this repository from my account, so if maintainers would rather review this as a pull request, say so and I will arrange a branch. ``` aiter/test_common.py | 64 +++++++++++++++++++ op_tests/test_checkallclose_strict.py | 101 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++ ```
Full patch (checkallclose-strict.patch, 240 lines) — git am applies it on 536118a ```diff From 673c7385942a90895367206519d5067e94d31119 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001 From: KHassanQazi <281752142+KHassanQazi@users.noreply.github.com> Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 18:05:39 -0400 Subject: [PATCH] test_common: add opt-in strict mode so checkAllclose can fail a test checkAllclose logs 'failed!' and returns the mismatch ratio. op_tests discard that return value, so a comparison failure never changes the process exit code and .github/scripts/aiter_test.sh reports the file as passed. Add a 'strict' argument, defaulting to the AITER_STRICT_ALLCLOSE environment variable, that raises AssertionError when the mismatch ratio exceeds tol_err_ratio. Default behaviour is unchanged. The environment variable is ignored on the printLog=False path so autotuners keep getting the ratio back instead of an exception. Co-authored-by: Cursor Signed-off-by: KHassanQazi <281752142+KHassanQazi@users.noreply.github.com> --- aiter/test_common.py | 64 ++++++++++++++++ op_tests/test_checkallclose_strict.py | 101 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++ 2 files changed, 165 insertions(+) create mode 100644 op_tests/test_checkallclose_strict.py diff --git a/aiter/test_common.py b/aiter/test_common.py index 75b0b3b..53b5587 100644 --- a/aiter/test_common.py +++ b/aiter/test_common.py @@ -409,6 +409,34 @@ def get_trace_perf(prof, num_iters): _CATASTROPHIC_REL_THRESHOLD = 0.5 +_STRICT_ALLCLOSE_ENV = "AITER_STRICT_ALLCLOSE" + + +def _strict_allclose_default(): + """Read ``AITER_STRICT_ALLCLOSE`` at call time, not import time. + + Read lazily so a test that sets the variable after importing + ``aiter.test_common`` still gets the intended behaviour, and so the + setting can be toggled per-process in the CI matrix. + """ + return os.environ.get(_STRICT_ALLCLOSE_ENV, "0").strip().lower() not in ( + "", + "0", + "false", + "no", + "off", + ) + + +def _strict_failure( + msg, percent, num, numel, rtol, atol, tol_err_ratio, max_delta=None +): + detail = "" if max_delta is None else f", max abs delta {max_delta:.6g}" + return AssertionError( + f"{msg}checkAllclose failed: {percent:.1%} ({num} of {numel}) elements " + f"exceed rtol={rtol} atol={atol}, above tol_err_ratio={tol_err_ratio}{detail}" + ) + def _relmag_catastrophic(actual_max_delta, b): """Relative-magnitude catastrophic heuristic. @@ -487,7 +515,24 @@ def checkAllclose( printLog=True, max_abs_delta=None, catastrophic_check=False, + strict=None, ): + """Compare ``a`` against reference ``b`` and return the mismatch ratio. + + ``strict`` controls whether exceeding ``tol_err_ratio`` raises instead of + only logging ``failed!``: + + * ``None`` (default) -- take the value from ``AITER_STRICT_ALLCLOSE``, but + only on the logging path. Autotuners call with ``printLog=False`` and + need the ratio returned so they can rank candidates, so the environment + variable never turns those call sites into exceptions. + * ``True`` / ``False`` -- explicit, and honoured on every path. + + A catastrophic mismatch raises regardless of ``strict``, as before. + """ + if strict is None: + strict = printLog and _strict_allclose_default() + isClose = torch.isclose(a, b, rtol=rtol, atol=atol) if isClose.all(): @@ -502,6 +547,10 @@ def checkAllclose( percent = (num / a.numel()).item() if not printLog: if percent >= tol_err_ratio: + if strict and percent > tol_err_ratio: + raise _strict_failure( + msg, percent, num, a.numel(), rtol, atol, tol_err_ratio + ) return percent is_cat = _catastrophic_check_silent( a, b, max_abs_delta, catastrophic_check @@ -517,6 +566,10 @@ def checkAllclose( percent = (num / a.numel()).item() if not printLog: if percent >= tol_err_ratio: + if strict and percent > tol_err_ratio: + raise _strict_failure( + msg, percent, num, a.numel(), rtol, atol, tol_err_ratio + ) return percent is_cat = _catastrophic_check_silent( a, b, max_abs_delta, catastrophic_check @@ -561,6 +614,17 @@ def checkAllclose( f"{msg}catastrophic error: max abs delta {actual_max_delta:.4f}, " f"{percent:.1%} ({num} of {a.numel()}) elements mismatch" ) + if strict and percent > tol_err_ratio: + raise _strict_failure( + msg, + percent, + num, + a.numel(), + rtol, + atol, + tol_err_ratio, + actual_max_delta, + ) return percent diff --git a/op_tests/test_checkallclose_strict.py b/op_tests/test_checkallclose_strict.py new file mode 100644 index 0000000..39f07e3 --- /dev/null +++ b/op_tests/test_checkallclose_strict.py @@ -0,0 +1,101 @@ +# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT +# Copyright (C) 2024-2026, Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. All rights reserved. +"""Behavioural contract for checkAllclose's strict mode. + +CPU-only and dependency-free beyond torch, so it runs anywhere the package +imports. Verifies that: + + * the default stays exactly as it is today (log, return the ratio), + * ``strict=True`` and ``AITER_STRICT_ALLCLOSE=1`` turn an over-threshold + mismatch into an ``AssertionError``, + * strict never fires on the autotuner path (``printLog=False``) or on a + mismatch that stays under ``tol_err_ratio``. +""" + +import os + +import torch + +from aiter.test_common import checkAllclose + +STRICT_ENV = "AITER_STRICT_ALLCLOSE" + + +def _pair(bad_rows=32, rows=64, cols=128): + torch.manual_seed(0) + ref = torch.randn(rows, cols) + out = ref.clone() + out[:bad_rows] += 10.0 + return out, ref + + +def _raises(**kwargs): + out, ref = _pair() + try: + checkAllclose(out, ref, **kwargs) + except AssertionError: + return True + return False + + +def test_default_logs_and_returns_ratio(): + os.environ.pop(STRICT_ENV, None) + out, ref = _pair() + ratio = checkAllclose(out, ref, msg="default: ") + assert ratio == 0.5, f"expected 0.5 mismatch ratio, got {ratio}" + + +def test_explicit_strict_raises(): + os.environ.pop(STRICT_ENV, None) + assert _raises(msg="explicit: ", strict=True) + + +def test_env_var_enables_strict(): + os.environ[STRICT_ENV] = "1" + try: + assert _raises(msg="env: ") + finally: + os.environ.pop(STRICT_ENV, None) + + +def test_env_var_does_not_affect_tuner_path(): + # Autotuners call with printLog=False and rank candidates by the returned + # ratio; the env var must not turn those into exceptions. + os.environ[STRICT_ENV] = "1" + try: + out, ref = _pair() + ratio = checkAllclose(out, ref, msg="tuner: ", printLog=False) + assert ratio == 0.5, f"expected 0.5 mismatch ratio, got {ratio}" + finally: + os.environ.pop(STRICT_ENV, None) + + +def test_strict_passes_when_close(): + os.environ[STRICT_ENV] = "1" + try: + torch.manual_seed(0) + ref = torch.randn(64, 128) + assert checkAllclose(ref.clone(), ref, msg="clean: ") == 0 + finally: + os.environ.pop(STRICT_ENV, None) + + +def test_strict_respects_tol_err_ratio(): + # One bad element in 8192 is under the 5% default, so it stays a warning. + os.environ[STRICT_ENV] = "1" + try: + torch.manual_seed(0) + ref = torch.randn(64, 128) + out = ref.clone() + out[0, 0] += 10.0 + checkAllclose(out, ref, msg="below-ratio: ") + finally: + os.environ.pop(STRICT_ENV, None) + + +if __name__ == "__main__": + for name, fn in sorted(globals().items()): + if name.startswith("test_") and callable(fn): + fn() + print(f"ok {name}") + print("all checkAllclose strict-mode tests passed") -- 2.54.0.windows.1 ```

body:
There's a mechanism in HIP to retrieve this; https://rocm.docs.amd.com/projects/HIP/en/latest/doxygen/html/group___global_defs.html#global-enum-and-defines:~:text=clock%20in%20kilohertz.-,hipDeviceAttributeNumberOfXccs%C2%A0,compute%20or%20memory).%20Partition%20modes%20can%20be%20set%20using%20amd%E2%80%91smi,-.

https://rocm.docs.amd.com/projects/HIP/en/latest/doxygen/html/group___global_defs.html#global-enum-and-defines

https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/2bd2056a5836f3840b55b1b05127642e8eaf1841/aiter/ops/triton/utils/device_info.py#L25-L27

Some sort of code like this could work;
```py
def get_num_xcc(device_id=None):
    if device_id is None:
        device_id = get_device_id()

    rocm_major, _ = get_rocm_version()
    if rocm_major < 7:
        return 8
    hipDeviceAttributeNumberOfXccs = 10018
    xcc_count = ctypes.c_int()
    gpu_try(gpu_runtime.hipDeviceGetAttribute(ctypes.byref(xcc_count), hipDeviceAttributeNumberOfXccs, device_id))
```

title: [MI355X][MegaMoEV2] GLM-5.2 EP8 tuning handoff and C14 performance gap
body:
## Goal

Handoff of the GLM-5.2-MXFP4 MegaMoEV2 integration and EP8 tuning for 8x MI355X. The tuned operator is faster than the untuned MegaMoEV2 path, but serving still trails the TP8/EP1 baseline and shows a pronounced concurrency-14 gap.

## Code branches

- AITER tuning: https://github.com/xiaobochen-amd/aiter/tree/feat/mi355x-mega-moe-v2
  - tuned commit: https://github.com/xiaobochen-amd/aiter/commit/70f50bb1082a7cb22b2fc0d48dc9f17bbb45906e
  - untuned parent/control: https://github.com/xiaobochen-amd/aiter/commit/7ed7dca54731fc6962ce3f166c28e64cf46d33b9
- SGLang integration: https://github.com/xiaobochen-amd/sglang/tree/feat/mi355x-aiter-megamoe-v2
  - commit: https://github.com/xiaobochen-amd/sglang/commit/b967661167d60bd96048756f111433dc2a07331e

The AITER branch contains:

- a GLM-specific `H=6144, I=2048, topk=8, local_experts=32, MTPR=256` static policy;
- tuned stage1 dispatch/tile choices and stage2 `block_n=128, persist=true, persist_cu=192`;
- 12 combine launch rules for token counts 1 through 96;
- unit tests and the multi-GPU sweep harness `op_tests/multigpu_tests/tune_mega_moe_v2.py`.

The SGLang branch contains the reusable AITER MegaMoEV2 workspace, Quark MXFP4 weight conversion, model wiring, and graph-safe decode/prefill allocation.

## Target environment

- 8x AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`), single node
- `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`
- TP8/EP8 MegaMoEV2, 256 routed experts, topk=8, one separate shared expert
- EAGLE: 5 speculative steps, 6 draft tokens, simulated acceptance length 3.61
- fixed serving workload: 32 requests, 1024 input tokens, 256 output tokens, seed 42, HiCache disabled, 16K chunked prefill

## Quick validation

```bash
# From the AITER checkout in an ROCm environment.
python3 -m pytest op_tests/flydsl_tests/test_mega_moe_config.py -q
# Expected: 4 passed.

# Isolated 8-GPU operator validation.
torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=8 \
  op_tests/multigpu_tests/test_mega_moe_v2.py \
  --network glm52 \
  --bs-list 1,4,6,8,12,16,24,32,48,64,96 \
  --max-tok-per-rank 256 --iters 100 --accuracy-max-bs 12

# Example parameter sweep.
torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=8 \
  op_tests/multigpu_tests/tune_mega_moe_v2.py \
  --network glm52 --tokens 1,4,6,12,24,48,96 \
  --max-tok-per-rank 256 --iters 50 --sweep dispatch-cu \
  --output-json /tmp/glm52-ep8-dispatch.json
```

## SGLang reproduction

Checkout both branches above, then launch the tuned arm. Replace the image/model paths as needed.

```bash
export IMAGE=rocm-llm-bench:latest
export MODEL=/path/to/GLM-5.2-MXFP4/snapshot
export SGL=/path/to/sglang
export AITER=/path/to/aiter

docker run -d --name glm52-ep8-tuned -w / \
  --network host --ipc=host --shm-size 32g \
  --device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri \
  --group-add video --group-add render \
  --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --ulimit memlock=-1:-1 \
  -v \"$SGL:/sglang\" -v \"$AITER:/aiter\" -v \"$MODEL:$MODEL:ro\" \
  -e PYTHONPATH=/sglang/python:/aiter \
  -e PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 -e GPU_ARCHS=gfx950 \
  -e AITER_JIT_DIR=/aiter/aiter/jit \
  -e AITER_USE_FLYDSL_MOE_SORTING=1 \
  -e SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 -e MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE=40G \
  -e SGLANG_AITER_MEGA_MOE_DECODE_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=256 \
  -e SGLANG_AITER_MEGA_MOE_PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=16384 \
  -e SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.61 \
  -e SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected \
  -e SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token \
  \"$IMAGE\" python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path \"$MODEL\" --served-model-name \"$MODEL\" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8899 --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 8 --ep-size 8 --moe-a2a-backend megamoe \
  --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend flydsl --dsa-decode-backend flydsl \
  --dsa-topk-backend aiter --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion \
  --enable-fused-qk-norm-rope \
  --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --max-running-requests 16 --cuda-graph-max-bs 16 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \
  --watchdog-timeout 1800
```

Wait for `/v1/models`, then benchmark each concurrency. Run one full discarded prewarm first; flush the radix cache before every run; report the median of three measured repeats.

```bash
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8899/v1/models >/dev/null

# Use seed 142 for one discarded prewarm, then seed 42 three times.
# Remove stale output first; ignore the first JSONL record when computing the median.
rm -f /tmp/c14.jsonl
for seed in 142 42 42 42; do
  until curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8899/flush_cache >/dev/null; do sleep 2; done
  docker run --rm --network host -w / \
    --device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri --group-add video --group-add render \
    -v \"$SGL:/sglang:ro\" -v \"$MODEL:$MODEL:ro\" \
    -e PYTHONPATH=/sglang/python -e PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 \
    \"$IMAGE\" python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
    --backend sglang --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8899 --model \"$MODEL\" \
    --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 \
    --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 14 \
    --seed \"$seed\" --disable-tqdm --output-file /tmp/c14.jsonl
done
```

For the matched SGLang TP8/EP1 baseline, restart the same server with `--ep-size 1`, and remove `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe` and `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`. Keep the graph envelope and benchmark protocol unchanged.

## Measured results

### Tuned vs untuned MegaMoEV2

- isolated cross-rank max E2E: **4.6% to 11.5% faster** across the measured token buckets;
- directional EAGLE-cycle estimate: **4.0% to 9.6% faster**;
- steady serving output throughput:
  - C8: 898.08 -> 922.45 tok/s (**+2.7%**);
  - C16: 1491.59 -> 1543.57 tok/s (**+3.5%**).

### Direct tuned EP8 vs TP8/EP1 baseline at C14

One discarded prewarm plus three measured runs, median reported:

- TP8/EP1 baseline: **1372.68 output tok/s**, mean TPOT **7.13 ms**;
- tuned TP8/EP8 MegaMoEV2: **1089.03 output tok/s**, mean TPOT **9.21 ms**;
- tuned EP8 remains **20.7% lower in output throughput** and **29.1% higher in TPOT**.

The first tuned measured repeat was a cold/JIT outlier at 746.63 tok/s; the following two repeats were stable at 1089.03 and 1089.76 tok/s. Baseline repeats were 1353.28, 1372.68, and 1376.50 tok/s.

## Interpretation and follow-up

The EP8 tuning is real, but it does not close the serving gap. Stage1 (fused dispatch + GEMM1) remains the main isolated MegaMoEV2 cost. Recommended next work:

1. investigate the C14 scheduling/graph cliff between the stronger C8 and C16 points;
2. split stage1 dispatch wait from GEMM1 and profile rank skew;
3. build an iso-semantic control using MORI dispatch + A16W4 fused MoE + combine with identical routing, EP, token shapes, and weight layout;
4. rerun the full C1/C2/C4/C8/C14/C16 cross-backend sweep after any kernel changes.

The existing synthetic fused-MoE control is useful directionally but is not iso-semantic: activation dtype, dispatch, weight layout, and shared-expert handling differ.

title: [Perf] pa_decode_sparse: BLOCK_K=64 is suboptimal above the CU count — up to +43 % on gfx950 with a load-dependent choice
body:
`pa_decode_sparse` hardcodes `BLOCK_K = 64` (attention/pa_decode_sparse.py, gfx950 gluon driver). On MI355X this is only the right choice while the launch fits on the CUs — above that, `BLOCK_K = 32` is faster by up to **43 %**, with identical numerics.

## Measurements

MI355X (gfx950), 64 heads, head_dim 512 (448 NoPE + 64 RoPE), packed fp8 cache, top-k 2048 per query, `has_invalid=False`. Times are the minimum of 5 rounds × 15 iterations.

| queries | K=64 | K=32 | better | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1–16 | 62–64 µs | 62–65 µs | K=64 | 0.4–1.2 % |
| 24 | 78.4 | 72.8 | **K=32** | 7.6 % |
| 28 / 30 / 32 | 73–77 | 90–96 | K=64 | 19.2 % |
| 34 / 36 | 122–131 | 103–116 | **K=32** | 12.9–18.6 % |
| 48 | 121.7 | 110.3 | **K=32** | 11.1 % |
| 60 / 64 | 131–134 | 165 | K=64 | 19.0–19.9 % |
| 68 / 72 | 204–207 | 170–193 | **K=32** | 6.0–21.6 % |
| 96 | 218.9 | 193.1 | **K=32** | 13.0 % |
| **128** | 264.5 | **186.9** | **K=32** | **41.5 %** |
| 192 | 403.2 | 354.2 | **K=32** | 13.8 % |
| 256 | 552.1 | 399.5 | **K=32** | 38.2 % |

Max abs deviation against a torch reference is 0.000061 for **both** variants — this is purely a scheduling effect, not a numerics tradeoff.

## Why it is not monotonic in `num_queries`

The switch tracks the number of CTAs, not the query count:

```
ctas = num_queries * num_splits * heads_blocks
```

`num_splits` comes from `_decode_num_splits`, so e.g. 32 queries can launch fewer CTAs than 34. Sorting the same data by `ctas` makes it monotonic, and the threshold lands exactly on the CU count (`get_num_sms()` = 256 here):

```
BLOCK_K = 32 if ctas > get_num_sms() else 64
```

This predicts **21 of 21** measured load points correctly. Intuition: while every CTA gets its own CU, the larger block (4 warps, 64 KB LDS) does more work per CU; once multiple waves are needed, the smaller block (2 warps, 32 KB) packs better and hides the gather latency.

## Suggested change

In the gfx950 driver, replace the constant with the rule above. Wired in, it stays within ±0.6 % of the per-point optimum from 24 queries upward:

| queries | vs fixed K=64 | vs per-point optimum |
|---|---|---|
| 24 | +7.7 % | +0.5 % |
| 48 | +10.9 % | +0.1 % |
| 96 | +12.8 % | +0.2 % |
| **128** | **+43.2 %** | +0.5 % |
| 192 | +13.4 % | +0.1 % |
| 256 | +39.0 % | −0.0 % |

Note that `num_splits` must be computed before `BLOCK_K` (it is currently derived after), and `get_num_sms()` should be hoisted to module scope — at 62 µs kernel time a per-call lookup is measurable in microbenchmarks, though not in production where the decode runs inside a CUDA graph.

## Things that did not help (same setup)

- `GSPT` (bytes per thread in the gather layout): 16 is optimal; 8 costs 14 %, 32 costs 45 % at K=64.
- `waves_per_eu` 1 / 2 / 4: −4 % / −4 % / −69 %.
- Cache modifier `.cs` instead of `.cg`: does not compile.
- Forcing `kv_splits`: the automatic choice is already optimal at 64+ queries; more splits cost up to 45 %.

Happy to open a PR if the rule looks right to you — and glad to re-measure on other shapes (different head counts, top-k, or a bf16 cache) if that would help.

title: [Bug] AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE_REDUCE: comment states the inverse default, and the switch is inert on the tuned-config path
body:
## Summary

In `aiter/ops/flydsl/moe_kernels.py`, the comment above the
`AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE_REDUCE` check states the opposite of what the code does,
and the switch has no effect on the tuned-config path at all.

## The comment contradicts the code

```python
# Debug: force stage2 to use the masked reduce epilogue instead of atomic
# accumulate. Enabled by default; set AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE_REDUCE=0 to opt out.
if os.environ.get("AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE_REDUCE", "0") == "1":
    mode = "reduce"
```

The comment says "Enabled by default; set `...=0` to opt out". The code
defaults to `"0"` and requires `="1"` to enable — the exact inverse. Anyone
following the comment will believe reduce is active when it is not, or try to
disable something that was never on.

## The switch does not reach the tuned path

Setting `AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE_REDUCE=1` does not change the kernel that actually
runs when a tuned config is used. `fused_moe.py` derives the accumulation mode
from the **kernel name** in the CSV:

```python
_kn2 = metadata.stage2.keywords.get("kernelName2", "")
_atomic = parse_g2_kname_any(_kn2)["atomic"]
...
accumulate=_atomic,
```

With `glm5_fp4_tuned_fmoe.csv` selected (GLM-5.3, MXFP4, `model_dim` 6144,
`inter_dim` 512, 257 experts, top-9), the rows for token counts 1–1024 name
atomic kernels, e.g.

```
flydsl_moe2_layout_afp4_wfp4_bf16_t64x128x128_atomic_nt_sbm64
```

Observed on MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, with `AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE_REDUCE=1`
set in the environment: the log keeps reporting the `_atomic_` kernels, and
`moe_sorting` still receives `accumulate=True`. The `mode = "reduce"` assignment
in `_flydsl_moe_stage2_impl` is downstream of the name-derived decision and does
not override it.

## Why it matters beyond the comment

The atomic epilogue accumulates with float atomics, which are not associative,
so stage 2 results depend on block scheduling order. That is a plausible
contributor to run-to-run variation at `temperature=0`. `AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE_REDUCE`
looks like the intended escape hatch for exactly that, but on the tuned path it
is inert — the only way we found to get a deterministic summation order is to
edit `kernelName2` in the CSV itself.

## Suggested fix

1. Correct the comment to match the default (`disabled unless set to 1`).
2. Either honour the environment override in the name-derived path in
   `fused_moe.py`, or state in the comment that it applies only when no tuned
   `kernelName2` is supplied.

title: deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits crashes with SIGFPE for ChunkK=64 on gfx950
body:
**`deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` crashes with SIGFPE for `ChunkK=64`**

On gfx950, calling the Gluon paged-MQA-logits kernel with `ChunkK=64` and
`KVBlockSize=16` terminates the process with `Floating point exception (core
dumped)`. The wrapper's own precondition accepts the combination:

```python
assert ChunkK % KVBlockSize == 0 or KVBlockSize % ChunkK == 0
# 64 % 16 == 0 -> passes
```

**Reproduction** (aiter 0.1.21.post1, ROCm 7.2.3, MI355X / gfx950):

```python
import torch
from aiter.ops.triton.attention.pa_mqa_logits import deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits

BLOCK, HEADS, DIM, CTX = 16, 32, 128, 131072
batch, next_n = 8, 5
nb = (CTX + BLOCK - 1) // BLOCK
q  = torch.randn(batch, next_n, HEADS, DIM, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
kv = torch.randn(nb, BLOCK, 1, DIM + 4, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(torch.uint8)
w  = torch.randn(batch * next_n, HEADS, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
cl = torch.full((batch,), CTX, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
bt = torch.arange(nb, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32).repeat(batch, 1)
out = torch.empty(batch * next_n, CTX, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)

deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits(q, kv, w, out, cl, bt, CTX,
                              Preshuffle=True, KVBlockSize=BLOCK,
                              ChunkK=64, WavePerEU=8)   # -> SIGFPE
```

`ChunkK` of 128, 256 and 512 all work with the same inputs.

**Context — why we tried it.** The call site in vLLM
(`rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`) hard-codes `ChunkK=256, WavePerEU=2`. Sweeping
those on GLM-5.3 (`index_n_heads=32`, `index_head_dim=128`, block size 16,
`index_topk=2048`) shows the defaults are not optimal for this shape:

| rows | ChunkK / WavePerEU | median | vs default |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 40 | 256 / 2 (default) | 0.0661 ms | — |
| 40 | **128 / 8** | **0.0544 ms** | **−17.7 %** |
| 320 | 256 / 2 (default) | 0.3770 ms | — |
| 320 | **128 / 8** | **0.3237 ms** | **−14.1 %** |

The trend points toward smaller `ChunkK`, which is why 64 was tried. Three
repeats per point, median reported; 8 warm-up calls; `torch.cuda.synchronize()`
around each timing window.

Two side notes from reading the wrapper:
* `WavePerEU` is overridden internally (to 4 or 1), but only under
  `if get_gfx() == "gfx1250"`. On gfx950 the caller's value stands.
* `WavePerEU=16` compiles but warns: *"failed to meet occupancy target given
  by 'amdgpu-waves-per-eu' … desired occupancy was 16, final occupancy is 8"*.

Happy to test a fix on gfx950.

title: [Perf] 0.1.21 slower than 0.1.19 for GLM-5.3 MXFP4 on gfx950 (−18 % prefill, −10 % throughput); FlyDSL MoE tuning?
body:
Field report on **0.1.21 vs 0.1.19 for GLM-5.3 (full, `glm_moe_dsa`) on 4x MI355X**, in case it is useful for the release notes: 0.1.21 is a consistent slowdown for us, with identical accuracy.

Setup: ROCm 7.2.3, vLLM fork (2026-08-27), Quark MXFP4 checkpoint (`amd/GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`), fp8 KV, MTP k=3, TP4, block size 16, same instance, same night, back to back:

| | 0.1.19 | 0.1.21 (+ flydsl 0.3.2) |
|---|---:|---:|
| prefill, 128k prompt | 13 461 tok/s | 11 013 tok/s (−18 %) |
| 900k-token needle prefill | 127 s | 136 s |
| decode, single stream | 119 / 127 tok/s | 110 / 110 tok/s |
| throughput, 64 concurrent | 619 / 631 tok/s | 559 / 566 tok/s (−10 %) |
| perplexity (held-out) | 1.31810 | 1.31809 |
| needles 30k–900k | 4/4 | 4/4 |

Our 0.1.19 image carries a locally tuned `a8w8_blockscale_tuned_gemm.csv` for the four attention/dense shapes of this model (untuned, those fell back to `libtype=torch`). 0.1.21 routes the MXFP4 MoE GEMMs through FlyDSL instead, so our tuning no longer applies — that is our working explanation for the gap, not a claim. Two questions:

1. Is there a tuner for the FlyDSL MoE kernels comparable to `aiter/utility/pretune.py` for `module_gemm_a8w8_blockscale_tune`, or config files (`AITER_CONFIG_FMOE` / `AITER_CONFIG_GROUPED_FMOE`) we should populate for gfx950 + these shapes (hidden 6144, 256 experts, top-8, intermediate 1536)?
2. Two packaging notes that cost us time, in case they help others: 0.1.21 requires `flydsl==0.3.2` (with 0.2.4 the MXFP4 MoE path dies in `mixed_moe_gemm_2stage_common.py` with `Operand 3 of operation "rocdl.raw.ptr.buffer.load" must be a Value (contained a None item)`, which looks like a Triton/Gluon problem but is not), and the `hipcc -v` workaround for ROCm 7.2 lives in aiter's own `aiter/jit/utils/cpp_extension.py`, so a wheel upgrade silently reverts it.

Happy to run any tuning flow you suggest and report numbers.

title: mhc_post silently computes wrong results when post_layer_mix / comb_res_mix are non-contiguous
body:
## Summary

`mhc_post` forwards only `x.stride(0)` and `residual.stride(0)` to the kernel.
`post_layer_mix` and `comb_res_mix` are addressed with hardcoded contiguous
arithmetic and are never validated, so passing a non-contiguous view for either
of them **silently produces wrong results** — no exception, no NaN, just numbers
that are off by ~1e4 in relative terms.

Same issue applies to `out`, whose row stride is hardcoded as
`hc_mult * hidden_size`.

## Where

`csrc/kernels/mhc_kernels.cu`, in `mhc_post`:

```cpp
int m = residual.size(0);
int hc_mult = residual.size(1);
int hidden_size = residual.size(2);
int x_stride = x.stride(0);
int residual_stride = residual.stride(0);
AITER_CHECK(hc_mult == 4, "hc_mult only supports 4");
```

Only `x` and `residual` have strides forwarded. Inside `mhc_post_kernel` the mix
tensors are indexed as:

```cpp
float post_mix_v = post_layer_mix[idx * hc_mult + warp_id];
for (int h = 0; h < hc_mult; h++) {
    comb_mix[h] = comb_res_mix[idx * hc_mult2 + h * hc_mult + warp_id];
}
```

and the output pointer assumes a fixed row stride:

```cpp
DTYPE_I* out_ptr = out + idx * hc_mult * hidden_size + k_offset;
```

These are plain global loads/stores with no bounds check and no stride
consultation, so a view with a different layout reads/writes the wrong elements.

## Reproduction

Standalone, no framework needed. bf16, `hidden_size=7168`, `hc_mult=4`, gfx950:

```python
import torch
from aiter.ops.mhc import mhc_post

HID, HC = 7168, 4

def ref(x, residual, post, comb):
    term2 = torch.bmm(comb.mT, residual.float())
    return (x.float().unsqueeze(-2) * post.unsqueeze(-1) + term2)

for m in (1, 512, 8192, 16384):
    x        = torch.randn(m, HID, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
    residual = torch.randn(m, HC, HID, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
    post     = torch.randn(m, HC, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")

    # non-contiguous comb: even columns of a 2x-wide buffer
    comb = torch.randn(m, HC, HC * 2, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")[:, :, ::2]
    assert not comb.is_contiguous()

    out = torch.empty_like(residual)
    mhc_post(out, x, residual, post, comb)          # no error raised
    torch.cuda.synchronize()

    r = ref(x, residual, post, comb)
    rel = ((out.float() - r).abs() / r.abs().clamp_min(1e-3)).max()
    print(f"m={m:6d}  contains_nan={torch.isnan(out).any().item()}  max_rel_err={rel:.3g}")
```

Observed on MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.0, torch 2.9.1:

```
m=     1  contains_nan=False  max_rel_err=7.84e+03
m=   512  contains_nan=False  max_rel_err=2.22e+04
m=  8192  contains_nan=False  max_rel_err=2.66e+04
m= 16384  contains_nan=False  max_rel_err=3.03e+04
```

Every `m` I swept (1, 8, 32, 128, 512, 1024, 2047, 2048, 2049, 4096, 8017, 8192,
16384) is wrong, and none of them produce NaN or raise — which is what makes this
hard to notice downstream.

With contiguous inputs the same sweep matches the reference to within bf16
rounding (max rel err 0.0048), including with `store_nt` forced to both 0 and 1,
so the compute path itself is fine.

## Why it is not caught today

`op_tests/test_mhc.py` builds every input with `torch.randn(...)`, so all tensors
are contiguous and this contract is never exercised.

## Environment

- MI355X, gfx950, ROCm 7.2.0, torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.0
- aiter at `456b92780c8b650c1e3e4b0fa1ca21f0d1fb363d` (`csrc/kernels/mhc_kernels.cu`
  byte-identical to that revision)

title: [Issue]: gemm_a8w8_blockscale (Triton) returns NaN when K/NUM_KSPLIT is not a multiple of BLOCK_SIZE_K (gfx1201 DEFAULT config, K=12800 -> vLLM garbage on R9700)
body:
### Problem Description

`aiter.ops.triton.gemm.basic.gemm_a8w8_blockscale` returns **NaN** on gfx1201 (Radeon AI PRO R9700) whenever the selected config's split-K partition is not a whole number of `BLOCK_SIZE_K` tiles.

`configs/gfx1201/triton/gemm/gemm_a8w8_blockscale/DEFAULT.json` uses `NUM_KSPLIT: 8` for `M_LEQ_8`. The wrapper sets `SPLITK_BLOCK_SIZE = cdiv(K, NUM_KSPLIT)`. For **K = 12800** (Qwen3-32B `down_proj` at TP=2) that is **1600**, which is not a multiple of `BLOCK_SIZE_K = 128` nor of the 128-wide scale group. Inside the kernel:

- `num_k_iter = tl.cdiv(SPLITK_BLOCK_SIZE, BLOCK_SIZE_K)` = 13 → each partition over-reads 64 columns into the next one (double counting), and the last partition reads past K;
- `offs_k_scale = (pid_k * SPLITK_BLOCK_SIZE) // GROUP_K` → misaligned scale index for odd `pid_k`.

Result: NaN for M ≤ 8. K = 5120 and K = 25600 (which divide by 8·128) are correct with the same config. With `NUM_KSPLIT=1` forced, K = 12800 is correct (relerr 2e-4 vs fp32 dequant reference).

End-to-end symptom: vLLM main with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` on gfx1201 selecting `AiterFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` for Qwen3-32B-FP8 (block 128×128) produces `"lo lo lo lo ..."` from the first decode step. Every other linear shape in that model matched vLLM's native Triton kernel to 2e-4; only `(N=5120, K=12800)` at M ≤ 8 diverged (relerr 0.06–inf).

The bug is probably arch-independent (any arch whose config picks a ksplit that does not divide K/BLOCK_SIZE_K), gfx1201 just hits it through `DEFAULT.json`.

### Reproduction

Stack: ROCm 10.1.0a20260822 wheel nightly (HIP 7.16), torch 2.15.0a0+rocm10.1.0a20260822, triton 3.8.0+git3f6e4113, aiter main @ 456b9278, gfx1201.

```python
import torch
from aiter.ops.triton.gemm.basic.gemm_a8w8_blockscale import gemm_a8w8_blockscale as g, _get_config
fp8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn; dev = "cuda"
def inputs(M, N, K):
    x = torch.randn(M, K, device=dev, dtype=torch.float16); w = torch.randn(N, K, device=dev, dtype=torch.float16)
    xs = (x.float().view(M, K//128, 128).abs().amax(-1)/448).clamp(min=1e-6)
    xq = (x.float().view(M, K//128, 128)/xs[..., None]).view(M, K).to(fp8)
    ws = (w.float().view(N//128, 128, K//128, 128).abs().amax((1, 3))/448).clamp(min=1e-6)
    wq = (w.float().view(N//128, 128, K//128, 128)/ws[:, None, :, None]).view(N, K).to(fp8)
    ref = (xq.float().view(M, K//128, 128)*xs[..., None]).view(M, K) @ (wq.float().view(N//128, 128, K//128, 128)*ws[:, None, :, None]).view(N, K).T
    return xq, xs.contiguous(), wq, ws.contiguous(), ref
for M in (1, 2, 4, 8, 16):
    xq, xs, wq, ws, ref = inputs(M, 5120, 12800)
    cfg, _ = _get_config(M, 5120, 12800, backend="triton")
    out = g(xq, wq, xs, ws, dtype=torch.float16)
    c1 = dict(cfg); c1["NUM_KSPLIT"] = 1
    out1 = g(xq, wq, xs, ws, dtype=torch.float16, config=c1)
    err = lambda o: ((o.float()-ref).norm()/ref.norm()).item()
    print(M, cfg["NUM_KSPLIT"], err(out), err(out1))
```
Output:
```
1 8 nan 0.0002
2 8 nan 0.0002
4 8 nan 0.0002
8 8 nan 0.0002
16 1 0.0002 0.0002
```

### Proposed fix

Clamp `NUM_KSPLIT` to the largest value that divides `K / BLOCK_SIZE_K` before computing `SPLITK_BLOCK_SIZE` (or make the kernel mask the partition boundary). Minimal wrapper-side version, verified to fix the repro and the vLLM garbage (Qwen3-32B-FP8 TP=2 on 2×R9700 goes from garbage to coherent, 27.2/78.0/204.3 tok/s at 1/3/8 streams vs 25.8/71.1/182.5 with vLLM's native kernel):

```diff
@@ def gemm_a8w8_blockscale(
     if y is None and (config["NUM_KSPLIT"] == 1 or not skip_reduce):
         y = torch.empty((M, N), dtype=dtype, device=x.device)
 
+    # Split-K partitions must be a whole number of BLOCK_SIZE_K tiles (and of the
+    # 128-wide scale groups); otherwise a partition straddles a K block and the
+    # kernel produces NaN/garbage (gfx1201 DEFAULT.json: N=5120, K=12800, M<=8,
+    # ksplit=8 -> 1600 per split). Fall back to the largest ksplit that divides cleanly.
+    _bk = int(config.get("BLOCK_SIZE_K", 128))
+    _ks = int(config.get("NUM_KSPLIT", 1))
+    while _ks > 1 and (K % (_ks * _bk) != 0):
+        _ks -= 1
+    if _ks != config.get("NUM_KSPLIT", 1):
+        config = dict(config)
+        config["NUM_KSPLIT"] = _ks
     config["SPLITK_BLOCK_SIZE"] = triton.cdiv(
         K, config["NUM_KSPLIT"]
     )  # How big each split_k partition is
```

The same `SPLITK_BLOCK_SIZE = cdiv(K, NUM_KSPLIT)` pattern also exists in `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_preshuffle` in the same file.

### Operating System
Ubuntu 24.04 (container), host kernel 7.0.0-rc2

### GPU
2× AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201)

### ROCm Version
10.1.0a20260822 (whl-multi-arch nightly)

title: [Bug] HIP RMSNorm corrupts row-boundary elements for odd hidden sizes
body:
### Problem Description

`aiter.rms_norm` produces incorrect results for odd FP16 hidden sizes on MI308X.

An adjacent aligned shape (`hidden_size=768`) passes, while
`hidden_size=769` corrupts column 0 of several following rows.

The failing path loads `module_rmsnorm_quant`, suggesting an unhandled
vectorized tail in the HIP RMSNorm fast path. The OPUS RMSNorm path and the
previous AITER implementation produce correct results for the same shape.





### Operating System

Linux

### CPU

Intel Xeon Platinum 8575C

### GPU

AMD MI308X

### ROCm Version

ROCm7.2.0

### ROCm Component

_No response_

### Steps to Reproduce

## Minimal Reproduction

```python
import importlib.metadata

import aiter
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def run_case(hidden_size: int) -> None:
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    x = torch.randn(7, hidden_size, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
    weight = torch.randn(hidden_size, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)

    expected = F.rms_norm(x, (hidden_size,), weight, eps=1e-6)
    actual = aiter.rms_norm(x, weight, 1e-6)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()

    close = torch.isclose(actual, expected, rtol=5e-2, atol=5e-2)
    mismatch = torch.nonzero(~close, as_tuple=False)
    max_abs_diff = (actual - expected).abs().max().item()

    print(
        f"hidden_size={hidden_size}: "
        f"mismatches={mismatch.tolist()}, max_abs_diff={max_abs_diff:.6f}"
    )
    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=5e-2, atol=5e-2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"AITER: {importlib.metadata.version('aiter')}")
    print(f"PyTorch: {torch.__version__}, ROCm: {torch.version.hip}")

    run_case(768)  # Aligned control: passes
    run_case(769)  # Odd hidden size: fails
```

## Observed Result

```text
AITER: 0.1.21.dev80+g987203ba5.d20260825
PyTorch: 2.9.1+git7e1940d, ROCm: 7.2.26015-fc0010cf6a

hidden_size=768: mismatches=[], max_abs_diff=0.000977
hidden_size=769: mismatches=[[1, 0], [3, 0], [5, 0]], max_abs_diff=0.511719

AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
Mismatched elements: 3 / 5383
Greatest absolute difference: 0.51171875
```

## Expected Result

Both aligned and odd hidden sizes should match the PyTorch RMSNorm reference.

title: [Perf] a8w8_blockscale tuned table for gfx950 appears to be generated without --splitK: re-tuning gains 13-61% on low-M shapes
body:
## Summary

The shipped `a8w8_blockscale_tuned_gemm.csv` appears to have been generated
without `--splitK`, leaving a large amount of performance on the table for
low-M shapes on gfx950. Re-tuning the same shapes **with** the flag improved
every one of them by 13–61 %.

## Evidence: two tables in the same repo disagree

```
a8w8_blockscale_tuned_gemm.csv    6809 of 6870 rows have splitK=0   (99.1 %)
a8w8_bpreshuffle_tuned_gemm.csv      6 of  598 rows have splitK=0   ( 1.0 %)
```

The bpreshuffle table was clearly tuned with splitK; the blockscale one was
not. That is consistent with how the flag is declared in
`aiter/utility/base_tuner.py`:

```python
self.parser.add_argument(
    "-k", "--splitK",
    action="store_true",     # default False, no `default=` given
    required=False,
    help="Use splitK kernels",
)
```

`store_true` without an explicit default means splitK kernels are skipped
unless someone remembers to pass `-k`. Nothing in `--help` signals that the
shipped table was produced without it.

## Impact on gfx950 low-M shapes

MI355X (256 CUs), GLM-5.3 projections (hidden 6144, 256 experts). Shipped table
vs. re-tuned with `--libtype all --splitK --compare --update_improved
--min_improvement_pct 3`:

| shape (M, N, K) | shipped | re-tuned | improvement |
|---|---|---|---|
| (1, 2624, 6144) | 20.42 µs | 8.01 µs | **60.8 %** |
| (1, 6144, 6144) | 20.67 µs | 11.00 µs | 46.8 % |
| (4, 6144, 6144) | 20.54 µs | 11.33 µs | 44.8 % |
| (16, 6144, 6144) | 19.82 µs | 11.41 µs | 42.4 % |
| (32, 6144, 6144) | 19.92 µs | 15.20 µs | 23.7 % |
| (48, 6144, 6144) | 24.84 µs | 20.66 µs | 16.8 % |

**24 of 24 shapes improved**, none regressed. Bandwidth on (1, 6144, 6144) goes
from 1900 GB/s to 3458 GB/s; the winning configs use `splitK=3`.

The mechanism is straightforward: at `NPerBlock=64` and N=6144 only 96
workgroups are launched on 256 CUs. The same kernel config reaches 5140 GB/s at
N=36864 (576 workgroups). It is a parallelism shortfall, and splitting K is
exactly the fix — but only if the search is allowed to consider it.

The effect fades where the shortfall does: re-tuning M=48…512 improved only 14
of 32 shapes, and at N=6144/K=6144 only M=48 and M=64. From roughly M≥72 there
is enough work to fill the machine.

End to end in vLLM (TP4, GLM-5.3, MXFP4 experts + fp8 attention), single-stream
decode went from 171.3 to 184.7 tok/s (median of 6), accuracy unchanged
(GSM8K 148/150 before and after).

## Suggestions

1. **Re-tune the shipped a8w8_blockscale table for gfx950 with `--splitK`.** I
   am happy to contribute the 38 rows I measured, or to re-run over a wider
   shape list if you prefer a single consistent sweep.
2. **Make the flag's absence visible.** Either default it to on for the tuning
   entry points, or note in `--help` that the shipped tables were generated
   without it. As it stands, a `store_true` with no default silently narrows the
   search space, and the resulting table looks fully tuned.

Environment: ROCm 7.2.3, MI355X (gfx950), AITER 0.1.19. I checked v0.1.21.post1
— the GLM CSVs there are byte-identical to ours, so this is not fixed by
upgrading.

title: [Bug] MoeSortingMultiPhaseKernel_P0_v1: missing lower bound on signed expert id causes GPU memory fault under EP (one-line fix)
body:
## Summary

`MoeSortingMultiPhaseKernel_P0_v1` reads the expert id out of `topk_ids` into a **signed** `IndexType` and only bounds-checks it from above:

```cpp
IndexType eid = x[j.value];        // IndexType = int (signed)
if(eid < kargs.num_experts)        // no lower bound
    p_expert_mesh[eid * mesh_stride + curr_token_id] = (curr_topk_id + 1) & 0xffff;
```

Under **expert parallelism** the ids of experts owned by other ranks can be negative. A negative `eid` still passes `eid < num_experts`, so `eid * mesh_stride` becomes a **negative offset** and the store writes *before* `p_expert_mesh` — GPU memory access fault.

This matches the observed behaviour exactly: it only ever reproduces with EP enabled, and never without it.

## Fix

```diff
-                if(eid < kargs.num_experts)
+                if(eid >= 0 && eid < kargs.num_experts)
```

One line. Verified on the exact configuration that used to abort every time (details below). The same unchecked pattern is worth auditing in the other `MoeSortingMultiPhaseKernel_*` phases.

## Symptom before the fix

8x MI355X, vLLM serving DeepSeek-V4-Pro (384 routed experts, top-6, MXFP4), DP8 + EP + DSpark speculative decoding, `--max-num-seqs 512`. All workers die during CUDA graph capture:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-3 (Agent handle: 0x...) on address 0x7f836a527000. Reason: Unknown.
```

`ROCr Debug Agent` with `--precise-memory` attributes it to:

```
void aiter::opus_moe_sorting_entry<
    aiter::MoeSortingMultiPhaseKernel_P0_v1<
        aiter::MoeSortingProblemMp<int, float, unsigned char, 4, true, false, true>>, ...>
code object: .../aiter/jit/module_moe_sorting_opus.so
 => <+1068>: s_or_b64 exec, exec, s[2:3]
```

## Verification

Same run, same flags, only the one-line change:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| memory access faults | 8 (every worker) | **0** |
| server startup | dies in CUDA graph capture | **READY** |
| GSM8K (200 samples, 5-shot) | n/a | **0.955** |
| decode TPOT (batch=1) | n/a | **13.4 ms** (30.6 ms without spec decode) |
| DSpark acceptance length | n/a | **2.66** |

The multi-phase path is fully exercised — no dispatch policy override, no reduction in `max_num_seqs`.

## What isolates it

| config | TP | MoE | max_num_seqs | before fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8 + EP | 8 | EP8 | 512 | ok |
| DP2xTP4 + EP | 4 | EP8 | 512 | ok |
| DP2xTP4, no EP | 4 | TP4 | 512 | ok |
| DP8 + EP, no spec decode | 1 | EP8 | 512 | ok |
| **DP8 + EP + spec decode** | **1** | EP8 | **512** | **fault** |
| DP8 + EP + spec decode | 1 | EP8 | 384 | ok |

`max_num_seqs` and the CUDA-graph requirement are secondary — they only control whether a batch that carries a negative expert id reaches this kernel.

## Notes for anyone digging further

- A standalone reproducer calling `moe_sorting(...)` directly did **not** trigger it (11 values of M, `num_local < M` variants, and CUDA-graph capture/replay divergence all clean). It needs the real multi-GPU EP traffic that produces the negative ids.
- Things that looked plausible but were **not** the cause: clamping the device-side token count to `kargs.tokens`; forcing `moe_sorting_mesh_byte_size` to 4; bounding the mesh write by `num_experts * kargs.mesh_stride`; clamping `total_elem`; `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0`.
- Separately, `P0_v2` recomputes `mesh_stride` from the run-time token count while the host sized the workspace (and placed `p_expert_cumsum` right after the mesh region) from `h.tokens`. Not the trigger here, but the host/device disagreement looks like a latent issue on its own.
- `moe_sorting_mesh_byte_size` switching the mesh element 4B -> 1B at `tokens_ >= 512` is intentional (`ws(512) == ws(128)` is self-consistent), and `dispatch_policy=1` returning 0 is intentional. An earlier revision of this report wrongly flagged both.

## Environment

- aiter: upstream `main` @ `65a2e34d`
- ROCm 7.2.4, torch `2.11.0+gitd0c8b1f` (hip 7.2.53211)
- 8x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950)
- Model: DeepSeek-V4-Pro (384 routed experts, top-6, MXFP4 experts), EP8

Happy to open a PR with the one-liner if useful.

title: GEMM tuners: an interrupted run loses everything (results are only written at the end)
body:
Tuners write `-o` / `-o2` only after every shape completes. A long run that is interrupted — machine reclaimed, container stopped, OOM, timeout — loses **all** results, including the shapes that had already finished.

On a shared machine this is the dominant cost of tuning: we lost multi-hour `--libtype all` runs repeatedly and ended up wrapping the tuner in an external chunking driver (6 shapes per invocation) purely to bound the loss.

**Proposal**: append each shape's winner (and its `-o2` candidates) as it completes and flush; on startup, skip shape keys already present in the output file. That is consistent with how `--compare/--update_improved` already reads the tuned file, gives `--resume` for free, and makes CI's `op_tune.sh` restartable.

Found while tuning GLM-5.2 on gfx950 (see #5262 for a related scalability fix from the same campaign).

title: Untuned-shape logging exists only for bf16 (AITER_TUNE_GEMM); fp8/blockscale/a4w4 have none
body:
`AITER_TUNE_GEMM=1` makes `tuned_gemm.py` append every missed `(M,N,K,bias,dtype,outdtype,scaleAB,bpreshuffle)` to `aiter/configs/bf16_untuned_gemm.csv` — exactly what you need to tune a real deployment. The fp8 per-token, block-scale and a4w4 families have no equivalent: they log `not found tuned config in <csv> … will use default config!` at INFO and write nothing.

Consequence: to collect the shapes a live engine actually dispatches you have to scrape INFO lines out of the server log and hand-write the untuned CSV — which is also how shape-key mistakes creep in (we found a deployment where the engine fuses two projections and dispatches N=2688 while the shipped table targets the unfused N=2624, so every row missed silently).

**Proposal**: give every GEMM family the same writer, keyed by that family's untuned schema — mirroring what `AITER_ONLINE_TUNE=1` already does for fused-MoE (`untuned_fmoe.csv`). Bonus: the same hook makes the model_configs workflow self-serve.

Related, from the same campaign: #5262, #5263, #5264, #5265, #5266.

title: JIT baton dead-holder check is ambiguous under --network host (pid + hostname collide across containers)
body:
The JIT build baton records the holder as pid + hostname. With `docker run --network host` — the normal way to run tuners — every container shares the host's hostname, and low pids (1, 100-104) exist inside **every** container. So after a container is killed mid-build, the leaked baton looks alive to the next container forever and its workers wait indefinitely:

```
[aiter] [pid=101 pname=SpawnPoolWorker-1] waiting for baton release at .../lock_module_gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle_cktile_tune
```

Two aggravating details:
- locks leak in **three nested layers** — `lock_module_*` at the cache root, `<module>/build/lock`, and `.ninja_lock`. Cleaning only the top one (the obvious one) leaves the build wedged.
- with a host-mounted build cache the leak survives container restarts, so the wedge is permanent until someone deletes the files by hand.

**Proposal**: include a boot id / container id / process start-time in the holder record so liveness can actually be decided, and clean the nested locks together when a stale baton is reclaimed.

title: One infeasible tune candidate fails every kernel in the module (ninja aborts the whole build)
body:
If a single candidate instance cannot compile, ninja fails the module and **every** candidate in that run is reported dead (`us=-1`, `errRatio=1.0`).

Concrete case on gfx950: a CK Tile instance with tile `256x256x512` needs 262144 B of LDS against the 163840 B limit —

```
error: local memory (262144) exceeds limit (163840) in 'ck_tile::kentry<1, ck_tile::Fla...'
```

— and took down all 38 kernels with it. The tuner then reports a full profile of dead rows with no indication of which instance was responsible; the real error is buried under thousands of `NUMA balancing` / `hipcc not support` warnings. It took several wasted runs to find it.

**Asks** (either helps a lot):
1. compile candidates in isolation, or let ninja continue past a failed TU and simply drop that candidate;
2. surface the failing instance name at the end of the run (`N candidates failed to compile: …`) instead of only in the middle of the build log.

Note for anyone hitting the same wall: the flatmm pipeline keeps **two** A-stages resident regardless of `DoubleSmemBuffer`, so the LDS need is `MTile*KTile*2` (×4 with dsm) — a feasibility filter using `MTile*KTile` alone lets the bomb through.

title: CK Tile tune livelocks: the JIT build counts against the per-task --timeout
MXFP4 MoE: CK-Tile stage-2 mis-indexes E8M0 scales when inter_dim % 256 != 0, returning silently wrong results
body:
## Summary

The CK-Tile 2-stage MXFP4 stage-2 kernel (`moe_cktile2stages_gemm2`) mis-indexes its E8M0
weight scales whenever `inter_dim` is not a multiple of 256, and returns a badly wrong
result. There is no error, no warning and no NaN in the common case: the model loads,
serves, is measurably faster than a padded-to-256 alternative, and only the output is
wrong.

This is reachable from a real configuration. A model with `moe_intermediate = 3072` at TP8
has a 384-wide per-partition intermediate, and vLLM's ROCm MXFP4 oracle allocates it
exactly when it aligns to 128 rather than 256.

## Affected configuration

* `QuantType.per_1x32`, `q_dtype_w = fp4x2`
* bf16/fp16 activations, `ActivationType.Swiglu` — the dispatch that `get_2stage_cfgs`
  sends to the CK-Tile 2-stage kernels
* `inter_dim % 256 != 0` (128, 384, 640 measured; 256, 512, 768 are fine)
* gfx950 (MI355X), aiter 0.1.19, flydsl 0.2.4

## Evidence

rel L2 of each stage against `torch_moe_stage1` / `torch_moe_stage2`, token=32,
model_dim=6144, block_m=32, split_k=2. Stage 2 is fed the *reference* stage-1 output, so
the two stages are isolated from each other:

```
E=256 topk=8                         E=129 topk=5
 inter     path    stage1    stage2   |   inter     path    stage1    stage2
   256   cktile  0.003933  0.004314   |     256   cktile  0.003972  0.003759
   256   flydsl  0.000003  0.004371   |     384   cktile  0.003925 10.239405  <-- broken
   384   cktile  0.003986 10.280723 <-|     512   cktile  0.003933  0.003769
   384   flydsl  0.000003  0.004304   |     640   cktile  0.003951  7.928027  <-- broken
   512   cktile  0.003995  0.004376   |     768   cktile  0.003947  0.003751
   512   flydsl  0.000008  0.004321   |
   640   cktile  0.003990  8.005772 <-|
   640   flydsl  0.000002  0.004379   |
   768   cktile  0.003996  0.004297   |
   768   flydsl  0.000004  0.004274   |
```

Stage 2 fails at exactly the non-256-aligned `inter_dim` values, at both expert
geometries. Stage 1 is unaffected. The FlyDSL a16w4 kernels, consuming the same
preshuffled weights and `e8m0_shuffle`d scales, are correct everywhere.

End to end through `fused_moe` with the production weight preparation
(`shuffle_weight(..., (16, 16))` + `e8m0_shuffle`), rel L2 against the torch reference:

```
inter_dim=128   18.193647
inter_dim=384   10.408027
inter_dim=640    7.897558
```

## Root cause

Stage 2 reduces over `inter_dim` and indexes its E8M0 weight scales in groups of 8 blocks
(8 x 32 = 256 elements). The host pads the scale group dimension up to a multiple of 8
(`shuffle_scale` / `e8m0_shuffle`), so when `inter_dim % 256 != 0` the scale tensor handed
to the kernel has a wider group stride than the kernel's indexing assumes, and stage 2
reads the wrong groups. Stage 1 reduces over `model_dim`, which is why it survives.

It is not merely a read of uninitialised pad bytes. Pre-filling the w2 scale pad with a
known byte before `e8m0_shuffle` changes the magnitude but does not remove the error:

```
 inter_dim   w2 scale pad        stage2
       384   uninitialised          nan
       384   0x7F (E8M0 1.0)  10.239370
       384   0x00              0.686312
       512   uninitialised     0.003771
       512   0x7F (E8M0 1.0)   0.003765
       512   0x00              0.003766
```

The uninitialised pad only decides *which* wrong scales are read; the mis-indexing is the
defect. (`aiter/ops/shuffle.py` allocating that pad with `torch.empty` and never writing
it is a separate, smaller problem — it makes the failure nondeterministic.)

## Why this is not caught today

`op_tests/flydsl_tests/test_flydsl_moe_a4w4.py` reports **PASS** on affected shapes. Its
verdict is `allclose` with `atol=1.0, rtol=0.05`, which absorbs an absolute error of ~8
across 99.7 % of elements. The `close%` column does move (100.0 % -> 99.7 %), so the
signal exists and is discarded. A ~1000x error regression is invisible to that gate.

## Suggested fix

The real fix is in the CK-Tile stage-2 scale indexing: it should use the padded group
stride the host actually produced, rather than deriving it from `inter_dim`. That source
is not part of this Python package, so I could not attempt it.

As a host-side mitigation I have opened #5232, which stops the broken shape from reaching
the kernel: `get_2stage_cfgs` steers non-256-aligned MXFP4 shapes onto the FlyDSL a16w4
kernels, which are correct at any 128-aligned `inter_dim`. That PR also initialises the
`shuffle_scale` pad and ships a regression test covering `inter_dim` in {128, 384, 640}.
If the kernel indexing is fixed instead, the guard in #5232 becomes dead and should be
dropped — I would prefer that outcome and am happy to close the PR in favour of a kernel
fix.

## Environment

* MI355X, gfx950
* aiter 0.1.19, flydsl 0.2.4, torch 2.12.0
* Reproduced with `fused_moe` directly (no vLLM) as well as end to end under vLLM 0.28.0

title: [CI] op_tests are always run as scripts, so 141 pytest test functions never execute
body:
`.github/scripts/aiter_test.sh:85` runs every file under `op_tests/` at depth 1 the same way:

    test_cmd=(timeout 60m python3 "$file")

`python3 <file>` executes module-level code and the `__main__` block. It does not collect or call
pytest-style `test_*` functions — that only happens under `pytest`, which this repository applies
to `op_tests/triton_tests/` alone (`triton-test.yaml:102`).

### Scale

Measured on `op_tests/test_*.py` at depth 1 (the exact set the standard shards run):

| | count |
|---|---|
| files defining pytest-style `test_*` functions | 114 / 125 |
| `test_*` functions and `Test*` classes defined | 431 |
| of those, called explicitly somewhere in their own file | 208 |
| **files with no call site at all** | **21** |
| **test functions in those files that never execute under CI** | **141** |

Those 21 files also carry 79 `@pytest.mark.parametrize` decorators, so the collected case count is
higher than 141; I have not measured it, and 141 is the conservative figure.

The largest are `test_mha_v4.py` (55 functions), `test_fhmoe.py` (17), `test_mla_v4_nm.py` (11),
`test_flydsl_grouped_gemm_gfx1250.py` (8), `test_gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle_pad_k.py` (7).

These files exit 0 having executed no test. CI records that as a pass.

### Why this keeps recurring

Authors write pytest-style tests because that is the normal shape for a Python project, and nothing
in the repository signals that CI will not run them. ROCm/aiter#5132 is the most recent instance:
it adds `test_sonicmoe_correctness` explicitly "so CI can discover it", and the case does not run.
Fixing it per-PR does not stop the next one.

### Proposed fix — select the runner from the file, do not assume it

    explicit path::node selector           -> pytest
    file defines test*/Test*               -> pytest
    no test*, but has a __main__ guard     -> python <file>
    neither                                -> skip, and say so

This logic already exists and has been exercised in this repository: the validator in
ROCm/aiter#4870 implements exactly this selection and records the choice as
`test_selection.runner` with a `runner_reason`. It selected correctly on an unseen target
(ROCm/aiter#5089) in an independent run. It can be lifted into `aiter_test.sh`.

### Rollout warning

Turning this on runs 141 test functions that have never executed. Some will fail — those are pre-existing
failures becoming visible, not new regressions, and treating them as a release blocker on day one
would be the wrong reading. Suggested sequence:

1. Land runner selection behind an env flag, defaulting to current behaviour.
2. Run one shard with it enabled and publish the list of newly-executing cases and their results.
3. Fix or `xfail` with an owner and a ticket, file by file.
4. Flip the default once the list is empty.

A separate, smaller point worth fixing regardless: several script-style op_tests print a failure
summary and still return normally, so a real failure exits 0. `op_tests/test_sonicmoe.py` is one
(`main()` prints "Some tests FAILED." and returns). Those are invisible to CI for a different
reason than the one above, and a sweep for missing `sys.exit(1)` is worth doing alongside.

---

_Edited: the original numbers said 23 files / 171 cases. A stricter recount — excluding files that reference a test name in a list or dict, or dispatch through `globals()`/`getattr` — gives 21 files / 141 functions. "Cases" was also the wrong word: those are top-level functions, and with 79 parametrize decorators among them the collected case count is higher. The mechanism is unchanged: `aiter_test.sh:85` runs `python3 <file>`, and a file with no `__main__` guard and no call site cannot invoke its own test functions._

title: Silent incorrectness in `fused_moe` with cloned FP4 weights/scales
body:
### Bug description

`fused_moe` produces numerically incorrect, non-deterministic results for identical FP4 weights when the weights/scales are clone, I'm guessing this is a bug in how the kernel handles tensor storage/layout rather than tensor values.

This came up in gpumode.com

### Dependencies

https://github.com/gpu-mode/kernelbot/blob/main/docker/amd-docker.Dockerfile

In particular using aiter at this recent commit

```
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/ROCm/aiter.git \
    && cd aiter \
    && git checkout f3be04a12a0cfd6b5e2c7a94edc774f1bc24460d \
```

### Repro

```python
  import torch, math
  import aiter
  from aiter import ActivationType, QuantType, dtypes
  from aiter.fused_moe import fused_moe
  from aiter.utility import fp4_utils
  from aiter.ops.shuffle import shuffle_weight

  E, d_hidden, d_expert, top_k, bs = 257, 4096, 1024, 9, 8
  d_hidden_pad = d_expert_pad = 1024  # already 256-aligned

  gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda"); gen.manual_seed(42)
  hidden = torch.randn((bs, d_hidden), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=gen)
  topk_ids = torch.randint(0, E, (bs, top_k), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
  topk_weights = torch.randn((bs, top_k), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32).softmax(dim=-1)

  gu_bf16 = torch.randn((E, 2*d_expert_pad, d_hidden_pad), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=gen)
  dn_bf16 = torch.randn((E, d_hidden_pad, d_expert_pad), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=gen)

  torch_quant = aiter.get_torch_quant(QuantType.per_1x32)
  gu_w, gu_s = torch_quant(gu_bf16, quant_dtype=dtypes.fp4x2)
  dn_w, dn_s = torch_quant(dn_bf16, quant_dtype=dtypes.fp4x2)
  gu_w = gu_w.view(E, 2*d_expert_pad, d_hidden_pad//2)
  dn_w = dn_w.view(E, d_hidden_pad, d_expert_pad//2)

  gu_shuf = shuffle_weight(gu_w, layout=(16,16))
  dn_shuf = shuffle_weight(dn_w, layout=(16,16))
  gu_s_shuf = fp4_utils.e8m0_shuffle(gu_s)
  dn_s_shuf = fp4_utils.e8m0_shuffle(dn_s)

  kwargs = dict(expert_mask=None, activation=ActivationType.Silu,
      quant_type=QuantType.per_1x32, doweight_stage1=False,
      w1_scale=gu_s_shuf, w2_scale=dn_s_shuf,
      a1_scale=None, a2_scale=None, hidden_pad=0, intermediate_pad=0)

  # Run with original tensors
  torch.cuda.synchronize()
  out_orig = fused_moe(hidden, gu_shuf, dn_shuf, topk_weights, topk_ids, **kwargs)
  torch.cuda.synchronize()

  # Run with cloned weights (same values, different memory)
  torch.cuda.synchronize()
  out_clone = fused_moe(hidden, gu_shuf.clone(), dn_shuf.clone(), topk_weights, topk_ids,
      **{**kwargs, "w1_scale": gu_s_shuf.clone(), "w2_scale": dn_s_shuf.clone()})
  torch.cuda.synchronize()

  diff = (out_orig - out_clone).abs()
  print(f"Max diff: {diff.max().item()}")  # Expected: ~0.01. Actual: ~4.3
  print(f"Mismatched elements: {(diff > 0.05).sum().item()}/{diff.numel()}")
  # BUG: cloned weights produce completely different results

```

title: [Bug]: MLA get_meta_param returns an lru_cache'd device tensor, corrupting the split indptr under CUDA graph replay
body:
### Problem Description

## Problem

`aiter/mla.py::get_meta_param` is decorated with `@functools.lru_cache` and returns `num_kv_splits_indptr`, a CUDA tensor it allocates. The cache entry is that tensor's only owner.

A CUDA/HIP graph that captures a cache *hit* records only the tensor's pointer, with no producing kernel. When the LRU later evicts that entry, the storage is freed back to the caching allocator and handed to a later allocation. Replay then reads whatever now lives at that address.

Eviction is routine on the decode path: `total_kv` is part of the cache key and changes almost every decode step, while entries captured into a graph are never looked up again (replay runs no host code), so they are exactly what an LRU discards first. On callers passing `ignore_total_kv=1`, `total_kv` cannot even affect the returned value, so it is a pure thrash key.

Caching the tensor looks unintended. #322 added `@lru_cache()` when the function returned two plain integers; #1233 added the `torch.arange` at the call site, outside the cache; #1390 folded the arange into the cached function and at the same time tightened the decorator to `maxsize=1`; #1445 widened that back to the default 128, which is what turns eviction of a captured entry from rare into likely.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (Noble Numbat)

### CPU

AMD EPYC 9575F 64-Core Processor

### GPU

AMD Instinct MI355X

### ROCm Version

ROCm7.2.4

### ROCm Component

_No response_

### Steps to Reproduce

Environment: MI355X (gfx950), single GPU, torch 2.10.0+rocm7.2.4, HIP 7.2.53211, aiter main d58537b70. No model or checkpoint needed.

Add [op_tests/test_mla_split_indptr_cudagraph.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31716125/test_mla_split_indptr_cudagraph.py)

```
pytest op_tests/test_mla_split_indptr_cudagraph.py -q

FAILED test_get_meta_param_indptr_survives_replay
AssertionError: split indptr corrupted after replay (bs=480, splits=8):
  [3072, 3080, 3088, 3096, ...] != [0, 8, 16, 24, ...]
```

Deterministic, 3/3 runs. The test warms the cache, captures a graph over a cache hit, churns the cache past its maxsize to force eviction, replays an unrelated graph in the same pool to reclaim the storage, then replays the first graph.

Two notes on reproducing:
- Only bs=480 reproduces. bs=8 passes either way; the hazard is allocation-size dependent, which is likely why it has survived in tree.
- The bs=480 pass only fails once bs=8 has run and been released. The test does both passes in order with a `gc.collect()` between them, so it is self-contained, but a hand-written snippet that skips the bs=8 pass will not reproduce.

The corrupted buffer is not a uniform shift: it holds a fragment of one arange followed by a fragment of another (`... 3832, 3840, 776, 784, ...`), i.e. a torn read across recycled storage rather than a merely stale buffer.

## Impact

`_fwd_kernel_stage2_asm` derives `num_valid_kv_splits` from these values and indexes `Mid_O` accordingly, so a corrupted indptr reads out of bounds.

We root-caused a `Memory access fault by GPU node-N ... Reason: Unknown` on a TP8 graph-capturing MLA decode workload to this: the faulting wavefront's address decoded to byte 0x7800000 = 480*8*16*512, one element past the end of `Mid_O` at exactly the bs=480 / splits=8 / nhead=16 geometry above.

To be precise about what is and is not demonstrated: the test reproduces the indptr corruption, not the memory fault. The step from corruption to fault is inferred from that address decode. Separately, the same fault signature still reproduces on one of our TP1 configurations with the fix applied, so either this fix is incomplete or there is a second producer of the same signature; that is not yet separated.

### (Optional for Linux users) Output of /opt/rocm/bin/rocminfo --support

<details>
<summary>rocminfo --support output</summary>

```
Paste output here
```

</details>


### Additional Information

_No response_
