title: [Bug] top_k_top_p_sampling_from_probs(deterministic=True) segfaults on gfx942 with some builds; original race attribution withdrawn
body:
### Summary

`csrc/cpp_itfs/utils.py` guards the *build* with a file lock but leaves both the **existence check**
and the **`dlopen`** outside it. With one process per GPU, several workers can observe
`lib.so` as existing while another is still writing it, and load a partially written object.

### The window

`csrc/cpp_itfs/utils.py` @ `main` `e9e1278b`:

```python
def run_lib(func_name, folder=None):                                   # :273
    ...
    lib = ctypes.CDLL(f"{BUILD_DIR}/{folder}/lib.so", os.RTLD_LAZY)    # :276   ← unlocked load
    return getattr(lib, func_name)

def not_built(folder):                                                 # :290
    return not os.path.exists(f"{BUILD_DIR}/{folder}/lib.so")          # :291   ← unlocked check

def compile_template_op(...):                                          # :294
    ...
    if not_built(folder):                                              # :310   ← check
        ...
        compile_lib(src_file, folder, includes, sources, cxxflags)     # :319   ← lock lives in here
    return run_lib(func_name, folder)                                  # :320   ← load
```

`mp_lock` (`:95`, `FileBaton`-based) is only entered inside `compile_lib` (`:269`). So the sequence
"exists? → no → build (locked)" is safe against duplicate compilation, but
"exists? → yes → `dlopen`" has no ordering relationship with another process's in-progress write,
and neither does the `run_lib` that follows a *successful* build in a different process.

### What we saw

8× MI325X (gfx942, ROCm 7.2.3), vLLM with 8 worker processes, first run after a fresh build cache.
**All 8 workers segfaulted** during sampler warm-up (8 identical traces: four within the same second, the remaining four as each reached the same point). The `cpp_itfs`-backed op we could identify on that path was
`top_k_top_p_sampling_from_probs` (native trace top frame `top_k_top_p_sampling_from_probs_<hash>`).
Our container filesystem is ephemeral, so every boot starts from an empty build cache and all
8 workers reach the op's first use together. Gating that op off (native sampler) removes the
crash; in the same boot, a module that goes through `aiter/jit/core.py`'s baton-locked path
(`module_custom_all_reduce`, rebuilt for gfx942 by all 8 workers) did not crash — consistent
with a race in this path rather than a miscompilation.

The window is generic to `compile_template_op`, not specific to the sampler.

### Suggested fix

Either:

**(a)** put check → compile → load inside the same `mp_lock`, or

**(b)** make the artifact appear atomically: compile to a temporary path in the same directory and
`os.rename()` it into place. `rename` within a filesystem is atomic, so `os.path.exists()` can never
observe a partial object and existing readers keep their mapping. This is cheaper than (a) because
it does not serialize the readers.

(b) also removes the need for the check and the load to agree about anything.

### Reproduction

1. Clear `$HOME/.aiter/build`.
2. Launch N processes (N ≥ 4) that all call the same `compile_template_op`-backed op at once.
3. Some fraction crash in the loader. It is timing-dependent; a slower filesystem widens the window.

### What we verified / did not verify

- **Verified:** the code shape above on `main` @ `e9e1278b`; that all 8 workers crashed on first use
  and that gating the op off removes the crash.
- **Not** verified: that we captured a partially-written `lib.so` in the act. The evidence is the
  code shape, the crash signature and the contrast with the baton-locked path, not a direct
  observation of the truncated file. We did not attempt `strace`/`ltrace` under load, nor a
  single-process pre-warm experiment.
- Related but distinct: #4819 touches the same `cpp_itfs` sampling family (missing hipcub includes
  under the ROCm 10 gate) — different problem, mentioning it only because it is the same directory.

title: # [gfx1250] FlyDSL MoE heuristic-fallback kernel fails to lower: `LLVM ERROR: Do not know how to expand this operator's operand!` (`raw.ptr.buffer.load.lds`)
body:
## Summary

On **gfx1250 (MI455)**, running DeepSeek-V4 (fp8) through SGLang, aiter's `fused_moe`
finds **no tuned FlyDSL config** for the MoE shape and takes the **heuristic FlyDSL
fallback**. The FlyDSL compiler then emits `llvm.amdgcn.raw.ptr.buffer.load.lds`, which the
gfx1250 LLVM backend cannot lower, aborting the process during CUDA-graph capture:

```
LLVM ERROR: Do not know how to expand this operator's operand!
Fatal Python error: Aborted
```

FlyDSL is the performant MoE path we want to use on gfx1250, so we're asking for a **real
fix** rather than staying on the older workaround aiter (see "Workaround" below).

## Environment

- GPU: AMD **MI455 / gfx1250**, ROCm **7.14**
- Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash, fp8 (e4m3), tp=1
- SGLang 0.5.18 (`79491a58`), image `henryx/xsgl:v0.5.18-rocm7_14-mi455-20260823-pr32754-trial1`
- flydsl 0.3.1

**aiter versions — crashes vs works:**

| aiter | Result |
|-------|--------|
| current `main` `fe4b72cd4` (2026-08-23) | ❌ crash |
| akao-amd/aiter `481127f5` (2026-08-19) | ❌ crash |
| ROCm/aiter `73f5e114` (#4955 "Force fp4gemm preshuffle to triton on gfx1250") | ❌ crash (this PR does **not** cover the MoE stage-1 FlyDSL path) |
| ROCm/aiter `d9e5ef7ce08ee7045d583aed768cff41aa9210fe` (#4406, 2026-07-29) | ✅ works (predates the gfx1250 FlyDSL MoE path; routes MoE elsewhere; pins flydsl 0.2.4) |

So the regression window is roughly `d9e5ef7` (good, 2026-07-29) → `481127f5`/`fe4b72cd4` (bad).

## Repro

Inside the container, on a crashing aiter (e.g. `fe4b72cd4`), launch dsv4:

```bash
SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 AITER_GROUPED_CONTIGUOUS_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=16 \
SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=max SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=0 \
SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 \
AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=0 SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE=0 \
ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_GROUPED_FORCE_SPLIT_K1=1 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code --tp 1 --attention-backend dsv4 --page-size 256 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.60 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
  --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --cuda-graph-max-bs 256 --max-running-requests 256 \
  --disable-radix-cache --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3
```

It aborts during decode CUDA-graph capture.

## What happens (log + traceback)

```
[aiter][fused_moe] no tuned FlyDSL config for
  ('gfx1250', 256, 256, 4096, 2048, 256, 6, <ActivationType.Silu>, 'torch.bfloat16',
   'torch.float8_e4m3fn', 'torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2', 'QuantType.per_1x32', True, False),
  using heuristic FlyDSL fallback
  (kn1='flydsl_moe1_afp8_wfp4_bf16_t32x128x256_w2_gui',
   kn2='flydsl_moe2_afp8_wfp4_bf16_t32x128x256_atomic_bnt2')

ExpandIntegerOperand Op #2: t197: ch = llvm.amdgcn.raw.ptr.buffer.load.lds<
  (dereferenceable load (s128) from ..., addrspace 8),
  (dereferenceable store (s4096) into ..., addrspace 3)> ...
LLVM ERROR: Do not know how to expand this operator's operand!
Fatal Python error: Aborted

  flydsl/compiler/jit_function.py:772  _run_pipeline
  flydsl/compiler/jit_function.py:924  compile
  aiter/ops/flydsl/moe_kernels.py:996   _run_compiled
  aiter/ops/flydsl/moe_kernels.py:1741  _flydsl_moe_stage1_impl
  aiter/ops/flydsl/moe_kernels.py:1942  flydsl_moe_stage1
  aiter/fused_moe.py:1451               _flydsl_stage1_wrapper
  ... (SGLang) ... decode_cuda_graph_runner capture ...
RuntimeError: Rank 0 scheduler died during initialization (exit code: -6)
```

## Root-cause pointers (aiter source, `fe4b72cd4`)

- `aiter/fused_moe.py:2774-2775` — the "no tuned FlyDSL config → heuristic FlyDSL fallback"
  branch in `get_2stage_cfgs` builds the fallback kernel names
  (`flydsl_moe1_afp8_wfp4_bf16_t32x128x256_w2_gui` / `flydsl_moe2_...`).
- `aiter/fused_moe.py:1451` `_flydsl_stage1_wrapper` → `aiter/ops/flydsl/moe_kernels.py:1884
  flydsl_moe_stage1` → `:607 compile_flydsl_moe_stage1` → flydsl JIT compile → the emitted
  IR contains `llvm.amdgcn.raw.ptr.buffer.load.lds`, which the gfx1250 backend can't expand.
- On gfx1250 the MoE path is FlyDSL-only (`fused_moe.py:799` gfx1250 branch), so there is no
  non-FlyDSL fallback to route around it — the heuristic FlyDSL kernel is what runs.

## Ask

Since FlyDSL is the intended high-performance MoE path on gfx1250, we'd like a real fix, in
rough order of preference:

1. **Fix the FlyDSL codegen/lowering on gfx1250** so the heuristic-fallback MoE kernel does
   not emit an un-lowerable `raw.ptr.buffer.load.lds` (or so the backend can lower it).
2. **Ship a tuned FlyDSL config for gfx1250** for this dsv4 MoE shape
   (`256, 256, 4096, 2048, 256, 6`, afp8/wfp4/bf16, per_1x32) so the heuristic fallback isn't
   hit in the first place — if the tuned kernels use a codegen path that already lowers.
3. If neither is near-term, at least make the fallback **fail gracefully / pick a lowerable
   kernel** on gfx1250 instead of aborting the whole scheduler.

Happy to test candidate fixes on our MI455 and report back.

## Notes

- **Grep tip**: the rocdl dialect prints the underscore form `raw_ptr_buffer_load_lds`, but
  the LLVM lowering failure prints the **dotted** form `raw.ptr.buffer.load.lds`. Match
  `raw[._]ptr[._]buffer[._]load[._]lds|Do not know how to expand this operator` to catch both.
- **Workaround (not a fix)**: pinning aiter to `d9e5ef7` (#4406) runs dsv4 (gsm8k 0.925/0.930,
  reproduced 2×) because that state doesn't route MoE through FlyDSL at all — but it forgoes
  later enhancements and the FlyDSL perf path, which is why we're filing this rather than
  staying on d9e5ef7.

title: [Feature Request] Expose a capabilities() API for runtime feature/version detection
body:
## Motivation

vLLM currently has no reliable way to ask "does this installed AITER build support feature X" -- so each call site invents its own detection method, several of them fragile:

- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py` reads AITER's shipped `.cu`/`.cuh` source files off disk and string-matches for dispatch cases (e.g. checking for `MLA_REDUCE_CASE_EF(NUM_HEAD,24,HEAD_DIM,512,` to detect native H24 reducer support, since the reducer and metadata planner have independent shape dispatch and there's no single source of truth for either).
- `vllm/_aiter_ops.py` uses `inspect.signature()` on `aiter.mla.mla_decode_fwd`, `aiter.topk_softmax`, and `aiter.fused_moe.fused_moe` to check for the presence of specific kwargs (`q_scale`/`kv_scale`, `num_shared_experts`, `gate_mode`) added in specific past PRs/versions.
- One of those (`topk_softmax`) has a documented fallback: `@compile_ops` erases the real Python signature, so detection falls through to parsing the compiled torch op's schema string instead.
- `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/aiter.py` does a plain `hasattr(aiter, "hipb_mm")`.

Separately, when deciding which AITER version to pin (e.g. the recent `v0.1.19` -> `v0.1.19.post2`/`v0.1.20` bump discussion on vllm-project/vllm#51728, continued on vllm-project/vllm#52826), maintainers had to manually diff git history -- checking whether a specific merge commit was an ancestor of a candidate tag -- to determine whether a needed fix was actually included. This came up independently for at least three different fixes/features (ROCm/aiter#4312, #4646, #4412) during that one version-bump discussion.

Both are the same underlying gap: there's no declared, queryable contract for what a given AITER build supports, so consumers reconstruct it after the fact from source text, Python introspection, or manual commit archaeology.

## Proposal

1. **Runtime capability dict.** `aiter.capabilities()` returns a `dict[str, bool]` of named features (e.g. `mla_reduce_h24_512`, `qk_norm_rope_stride_aware`, `topk_softmax_fused_sigmoid`, `fused_moe_gate_mode`, `linear_hipb_mm`), maintained by kernel authors as a one-line addition when a feature lands -- replacing the ad hoc introspection above with a single lookup.
2. **Per-release manifest (optional, addresses the version-pin case).** Publish the same flag set as static metadata per tagged release, so a consumer deciding which tag to pin against can check "does tag X have feature Y" without installing/building it or diffing commit ancestry by hand.

## Relationship to existing discussion

This is a narrower, more mechanical instance of the "layout capability negotiation API" question raised as an open item in #3885 -- that RFC is scoped to physical layout (weights/KV-cache/quant), which is a harder, structural problem. This proposal doesn't attempt to solve that; it's meant to be small enough to ship independently (rough estimate: ~2 days in aiter, ~1 day updating the vLLM call sites above to consume it) while still being a working example of the same shape of fix, in case that's useful groundwork for the bigger discussion.

## Open questions

- Right granularity for flag names -- per-function, per-kernel-file, or something coarser?
- Where should the dict live / how is it kept in sync with actual kernel code (hand-maintained vs. some lint/CI check)?

title: [Issue]: [FlyDSL][MoE][VLLM] moe_gemm_2stage: `fx.ptrtoint` on `!fly.memref` fails to build on gfx9500(MI355)
body:
### Problem Description

The FlyDSL **W4A16 (int4_w4a16 / a16wi4) fused-MoE** kernel in
`aiter/ops/flydsl/kernels/moe_gemm_2stage.py` fails to **compile** on gfx950
(MI355X). Its buffer arguments are annotated as `Pointer`, but the invocation
passes tensors, which lower to `!fly.memref`. `_ptr_buffer_resource` then calls
`fx.ptrtoint(...)` on that memref, and FlyDSL's `PtrToIntOp` rejects it (it
requires a `PointerType`):

```
flydsl._mlir._mlir_libs._mlir.ir.MLIRError: Operation creation failed:
  error: "addr = fx.ptrtoint(ptr)"
  (".../aiter/ops/flydsl/kernels/moe_gemm_2stage.py":386:15):
  PtrToIntOp: expected PointerType, got '!fly.memref<si32, global, ?:1>'
```

This is a deterministic, build-time bug (before any kernel launch). It
reproduces across **every** aiter + flydsl combination we tried, including aiter
`main` — a version bump does not fix it.

### Offending code

`aiter/ops/flydsl/kernels/moe_gemm_2stage.py` (~line 386):

```python
def _ptr_buffer_resource(ptr, num_records_bytes):
    addr = fx.ptrtoint(ptr)          # ptr resolves to a !fly.memref, not a pointer
    addr_i64 = arith.index_cast(T.i64, addr)
    return buffer_ops.create_buffer_resource_from_addr(
        addr_i64, num_records_bytes=num_records_bytes
    )
```

### Root cause

The MoE `@jit`/`@kernel` buffer params (`arg_x`, `arg_w`, `arg_out`,
`arg_scale_*`, `arg_sorted_*`, `arg_expert_ids`, ...) are annotated as `Pointer`
but the invocation passes **tensors**, which lower to `!fly.memref`. Under flydsl
0.2.4 this is visible as:

```
UserWarning: @jit parameter 'arg_x'   is annotated as 'Pointer', but the argument resolves to 'Tensor' ...
UserWarning: @jit parameter 'arg_out' is annotated as 'Pointer', but the argument resolves to 'Tensor' ...
```

`_ptr_buffer_resource` then does `fx.ptrtoint(memref)`, which no FlyDSL version
accepts. The defect is at the invocation boundary — specifically the MoE
**stage1** path, which deliberately uses dynamic memrefs (source comment:
"stage1 uses dynamic memrefs so they are ignored").



### Operating System

NAME="Ubuntu" VERSION="22.04.5 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish)"

### CPU

AMD EPYC 9575F 64-Core

### GPU

amdgcn-amd-amdhsa--gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-

### ROCm Version

ROCm 7.2.3

### ROCm Component

_No response_

### Steps to Reproduce


### Container image (how to reproduce the exact environment)
We hit this in the **vLLM ROCm image** built from `vllm/docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base`:
- `BASE_IMAGE=rocm/dev-ubuntu-22.04:7.2.3-complete`
- aiter is **built from source** in the image:
  `AITER_REPO=https://github.com/ROCm/aiter.git`, `AITER_BRANCH=v0.1.16.post3`
  (`git clone --recursive --branch v0.1.16.post3`)
- flydsl (`0.2.0`) is pulled transitively by aiter
- `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH` includes `gfx950`
The final image records these under `/app/versions.txt` (`BASE_IMAGE`,
`AITER_BRANCH`, `AITER_REPO`, ...). To reproduce, build that image (or any ROCm
7.2.x + Python 3.12 env) with aiter `v0.1.16.post3` from source on gfx950.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a gfx950 host with the environment above (aiter `v0.1.16.post3` +
   flydsl `0.2.0`; see the image recipe in the Environment section).
2. Ensure a **cold** FlyDSL JIT cache — use a fresh container or clear the
   flydsl JIT cache.
3. Build/invoke the W4A16 MoE kernel via the `int4_w4a16` (a16wi4) path, with
   buffers passed as torch tensors (as the downstream does). Minimal entry point:

   ```python
   from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels.moe_gemm_2stage import compile_moe_gemm1
   # invoke/compile the int4_w4a16 gemm1 kernel with torch tensors as buffers
   ```

4. Kernel build fails with the `PtrToIntOp: expected PointerType, got
   '!fly.memref<...>'` MLIRError shown above.

### Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** the W4A16 MoE kernel builds and runs on gfx950.
- **Actual:** MLIR op construction fails at `fx.ptrtoint` because the argument is
  a `!fly.memref`, not a `PointerType`.

### (Optional for Linux users) Output of /opt/rocm/bin/rocminfo --support

<details>
<summary>rocminfo --support output</summary>

```
Paste output here
```

</details>


### Additional Information

### Version matrix — no combination works

Built each aiter from source (`setup.py develop`, `GPU_ARCHS=gfx950`) on gfx950;
each pulls its own pinned flydsl:

| aiter (from source)        | flydsl | result                                              |
|----------------------------|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| v0.1.16.post3              | 0.2.0  | FAIL — `ptrtoint(memref)` @ moe_gemm_2stage.py:386  |
| v0.1.17                    | 0.2.2  | FAIL — identical error                              |
| main (0.1.1.dev1+gd85eb69) | 0.2.4  | FAIL — identical error                              |

flydsl-only sweep on the v0.1.16.post3 kernel (0.2.0 / 0.2.2 / 0.2.4): all FAIL
identically. We also built the fork change #3373 ("use fx.ptr for kernels not
using layout"): still FAIL — it targets kernels **not** using layout, whereas MoE
stage1 deliberately uses dynamic memrefs.

### What we're asking

1. Please confirm this is an upstream aiter bug in the MoE stage1
   dynamic-memref path.
2. A proper fix so the kernel receives a real `fx.ptr` (or converts the dynamic
   memref to a pointer before `ptrtoint`, or avoids `ptrtoint` on memrefs) on the
   int4_w4a16 / a16wi4 path.
3. The aiter release/tag that will carry the fix, so downstreams can pin to it.

### Additional context

Diagnostic only (not a proposed fix): routing memref inputs through
`buffer_ops.extract_base_index` instead of `fx.ptrtoint` lets all parametrizations
build and produce numerically-correct output. This confirms the *only* broken
thing is the `ptrtoint(memref)` lowering; the kernel math is otherwise correct.

title: [Issue]: bf16 GEMM asm kernels crash with GPU memory access fault on skinny M=1 shapes (gfx950)
body:
### Problem Description

## Summary

Several AITER assembly `bf16gemm_fp32bf16_tn_*` kernels (gfx950) abort the process with a GPU memory access fault for a subset of skinny `(M, N, K)` shapes where `M` is small and `K` is small:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-N (Agent handle: 0x...) on address 0x.... Reason: Unknown.
```

Reproduced and characterized on two independent single-GPU runs (device 0 and device 1); not root-caused. Found while tuning dense bf16 GEMM shapes for a Kimi-K3 TP=8 deployment: of 93 shapes, 1 (`M=1, N=1536, K=128`) hits this fault, but that's enough to abort the whole tuning run.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 22.04.2 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish)

### CPU

AMD EPYC 9965 192-Core Processor

### GPU

AMD Instinct MI350X VF, `gfx950`, 256 CU

### ROCm Component

_No response_

### Steps to Reproduce


## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| torch | `2.12.0+git6bbd260` |
| AITER | `0.1.21.post2` (wheel); also reproduces on `main` @ `0.1.23.dev142+g4927f8f5c` (editable install, 2026-09-23) |
| Image | `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm@sha256:f169e8df365b5112a1e6500543e13d8161374277c22c94d8ed60817324c101e1` |

Confirmed on the newly installed wheel and reproduces identically on two different physical GPUs (`HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` → KFD node-2, agent `0x19172300`; `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1` → KFD node-3, agent `0x1a661710`), single process (`--mp 1`), so it is not a multi-GPU/multiprocessing artifact.

## Reproduction

```bash
python3 csrc/gemm_a16w16/gemm_a16w16_tune.py \
    --mp 1 --timeout 120 --libtype asm \
    --input_file <one-row.csv> --tuned_file <out.csv> --profile_file <prof.csv>
```
with the input CSV:
```
M,N,K,bias,dtype,outdtype,scaleAB,bpreshuffle
1,1536,128,False,torch.bfloat16,torch.bfloat16,False,False
```

Fails in ~70-130s with:
```
[aiter] LoadKernel: _ZN5aiter39bf16gemm_fp32bf16_tn_32x64_splitk_cleanE hsaco: .../bf16gemm_fp32bf16_tn_32x64_splitk_clean.co
Memory access fault by GPU node-3 (Agent handle: 0x...) on address 0x.... Reason: Unknown.
```

## Characterization

- **M sweep** (N=1536, K=128): only **M=1** faults; M=2..4096 all OK on the identical `32x64_splitk_clean` kernel/grid.
- **N sweep** (M=1, K=128): faults at N ∈ {256, 768, 1280, 1536, 3072}, clean at N ∈ {64, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096}.
- **K sweep** (M=1, N=1536): faults at K ∈ {64, 128}, clean at K ∈ {192, 256, 384, 512, 7168}. K=64 faults on a different kernel (`32x64_pf3_splitk`) and at both M=1 and M=2, suggesting more than one fault mode.

## Hypothesis (untested)

Out-of-range read of the A operand (1×K bf16, far smaller than the kernel's M-tile of 32) — doesn't fully explain why only some N values fault, or why K=64 faults on a different, non-splitK kernel. Worth checking the M-bound predication on the A load in `bf16gemm_fp32bf16_tn_32x64_splitk_clean` under `rocgdb`/`AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3`.

## Workaround

Excluding asm from tuning (`--libtype flydsl,opus,triton,torch,skinny`) avoids the fault entirely; other backends produce a clean tune (at the cost of whatever asm would have won on these shapes).

title: [Triton/Gluon] Productize FMHA kernels in GFX950 Gluon Tutorial
body:
[ROCm/gfx950-gluon-tutorials](https://github.com/ROCm/gfx950-gluon-tutorials) has two GFX950 Gluon flash-attention forward kernels ([fmha_v3](https://github.com/ROCm/gfx950-gluon-tutorials/blob/main/kernels/attention/fmha_v3.py) and [fmha_v4](https://github.com/ROCm/gfx950-gluon-tutorials/blob/main/kernels/attention/fmha_v4.py)) with a series of optimization techniques which have proven good performance.

Productize these kernels into AiTER, so that the techniques could land in the current [`_gluon_kernels/gfx950/attention/mha.py`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/main/aiter/ops/triton/_gluon_kernels/gfx950/attention/mha.py) for expected performance and ease of further maintainance.
